rationale:
Decision: split into five children. Each one reuses an accepted DAG declaration with a byte-identical frozen Lean type, so no new child proof work is created.

Why this split.
- This node's frozen type and statement are byte-identical to those of the DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.null_sets-a1 (cmr_null_of_representation).
- Its supplied natural proof is also identical apart from the opening 'Source' line, so all step numbers coincide.
- The proof contains five independent, reusable obligations. That node's decomposition already produced, reviewed and accepted them:
  - step 3, Hausdorff-null sets have Lebesgue-null coordinate projections: proj_null = cmr_volume_coordProj_image_null;
  - step 4, the current/mass estimate for the representation integral against dη − ζ: div_mass_bound = cmr_abs_integral_div_le_mass;
  - steps 5–6, distributional localization: localize_null = cmr_ae_zero_of_div_bounds;
  - step 8, the mass measure vanishes where ξ vanishes: orient_zero_null = cmr_measure_null_of_orient_ae_zero;
  - step 9, inner-regularity extension from compact to arbitrary null sets: compact_to_general = cmr_null_of_compact_null.
- Without the split, this node's implementer would have to re-prove roughly 230 Lean lines that already exist, because other branches' theorems are not in its proof base. With the split, only the short assembly remains.

Sibling content enters the children as hypotheses:
- (EB) in div_mass_bound;
- (TD) and (DB) in localize_null;
- divergence_form's η/ζ as data in div_mass_bound.
So no child depends on the still-decomposing dimred siblings. Every depends_on is [] and the graph is acyclic.

What the parent keeps (about 70 Lean lines; steps 1, 2 and 7):
1. n = 0: μHE[0] = μH[0] and singletons have μH[0]-measure 1, so a μHE[0]-null set is empty.
2. n = m+1: apply compact_to_general with ν := μHE[n]. For a compact Hⁿ-null C ⊆ U, choose an open W ⊇ C whose closure is compact and contained in U. Either exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure or the thickening of step 2 works. Then μ(W), M_W(T) = μ(W) and M_W(∂T) = boundaryMassOn T W are all finite.
3. For each strictly increasing I, with θ_I from dimred_mbl_fnd_coordinate_covectors_span (a):
   - proj_null gives volume(q_I(C)) = 0.
   - Apply localize_null with f = ξ(·)(θ_I), q = q_I, N = q_I(C) (compact) and c = |θ_I|.
   - (TD) is dimred_mbl_fnd_null_of_div_bound with X = ℝ^P.
   - (DB) comes from dimred_mbl_fnd_coordinate_divergence_form plus div_mass_bound, with D = div g∘q_I and (EB) given by cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn.
   - Since C ⊆ W and q_I(C) = N, this gives ξ(θ_I) = 0 μ-a.e. on C.
4. Part (b) of coordinate_covectors, with ae_all_iff over the finite set Fin n → Fin P, gives ξ = 0 μ-a.e. on C. Any θ with the determinant formula equals θ_I by ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext.
5. orient_zero_null gives μ(C) = 0.

(i) Reuse admissibility, under the runtime's _existing_lean_name_problem and _accepted_checkpoint rules. Each name is held by exactly one DAG node, and that node has:

(iv) The five accepted commits' theorems were merged into one Submission copy. A check theorem using the real Submission.cmr_* declarations, with sibling stand-ins, proves the parent type with the same axioms. The only sorry is the pre-existing main_theorem.
(v) A fresh independent reviewer agent repeated (i)–(iv). It wrote its own assembly and an end-to-end proof from the real children, ran #check on all 57 cited names, and found each child proof complete and faithful to parent steps 3, 4, 5–6, 8 and 9. Verdict: ACCEPT.

subproblems.title: Coordinate projections of Hⁿ-null sets are Lebesgue-null (parent step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let I : Fin n → Fin P be injective, and let C ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P) satisfy μHE[n](C) = 0. Let q : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ (Euclid n) be the coordinate projection q(x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => x (I k)), i.e. q(x)_k = x_{I(k)}. Then the image q(C) has Lebesgue measure zero: volume(q(C)) = 0 (volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (I : Fin n → Fin P) (C : Set (Euclid P)), Function.Injective I → μHE[n] C = 0 → volume ((fun x : Euclid P => (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => x (I k)) : Euclid n)) '' C) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3, stated for an arbitrary injective I and an arbitrary set C (compactness of C is not needed).
Notation: q(x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => x (I k)), so (q x) k = x (I k). For d ∈ ℕ, μH[d] is the d-dimensional Hausdorff measure. By Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, on every Borel (e)metric space μHE[d] = c_d • μH[d], where c_d := addHaarScalarFactor (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) μH[d] ∈ ℝ≥0 is one fixed constant that does not depend on the space.
1. (q is 1-Lipschitz.) Let x, y ∈ ℝ^P. By EuclideanSpace.dist_eq, dist(q x, q y) = √(Σ_{k : Fin n} dist(x (I k), y (I k))²) and dist(x, y) = √(Σ_{l : Fin P} dist(x l, y l)²). Because I is injective, Finset.sum_image rewrites Σ_k dist(x (I k), y (I k))² as Σ_{l ∈ Finset.univ.image I} dist(x l, y l)². Every term is a square, hence ≥ 0, and Finset.univ.image I ⊆ Finset.univ, so Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg bounds this sum by Σ_l dist(x l, y l)². Monotonicity of the square root (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt) gives dist(q x, q y) ≤ 1 · dist(x, y). Hence LipschitzWith 1 q (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul).
2. (μH[n](C) = 0.) By the formula recalled above, 0 = μHE[n](C) = (c_n : ℝ≥0∞) · μH[n](C) (Measure.smul_apply, ENNReal.smul_def). By Measure.addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero n we have c_n ≠ 0, hence (c_n : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0, and therefore μH[n](C) = 0.
3. (μH[n](q(C)) = 0.) LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, applied to the 1-Lipschitz map q of step 1 with d = (n : ℝ) ≥ 0, gives μH[n](q(C)) ≤ 1^n · μH[n](C) = 0 by step 2. So μH[n](q(C)) = 0.
4. (Conclusion.) On ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n gives volume = μHE[n] = c_n • μH[n]. Therefore volume(q(C)) = c_n • μH[n](q(C)) = c_n • 0 = 0 by step 3.
proof_key_steps: q_I is 1-Lipschitz: for injective I the sum of squared coordinate differences over image(I) is at most the full sum.
μHE[n] = c_n • μH[n] with c_n ≠ 0 (same constant on every space), so μH[n](C) = 0.
The Lipschitz image bound gives μH[n](q(C)) ≤ 1^n μH[n](C) = 0.
On ℝⁿ, volume = μHE[n] = c_n • μH[n], hence volume(q(C)) = 0.

subproblems.title: Mass bound for the representation integral against dη − ζ (parent step 4)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U, W ⊆ ℝ^P with W ⊆ U, and T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U (m+1)) with M_W(T) := T.massOn W ≠ ∞ and M_W(∂T) := T.boundary.massOn W ≠ ∞. Let μ be a measure on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{m+1} (MultiVector P (m+1)) with T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U). Assume the evaluation bound (EB): for every k ∈ ℕ, S ∈ 𝒟_k(U), ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) and r ∈ ℝ with S.massOn W ≠ ∞, tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ r for all x, one has |S(ω)| ≤ r·(S.massOn W).toReal. Let θ be an (m+1)-covector, b, D : ℝ^P → ℝ with tsupport b ⊆ W, K ∈ ℝ, and let η, ζ be test forms (IsTestForm: smooth with compact support) of degrees m and m+1 with tsupport η ⊆ tsupport b, tsupport ζ ⊆ tsupport b, covectorEuclideanNorm(η(x)) ≤ K and covectorEuclideanNorm(ζ(x)) ≤ K for all x, and exteriorDerivative η x = (b(x)·D(x))•θ + ζ(x) for all x. Then |∫ b(x)·ξ(x)(θ)·D(x) d(μ.restrict W)(x)| ≤ K·((T.boundary.massOn W).toReal + (T.massOn W).toReal).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (m + 1)) (θ : Covector (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (b D : Euclid P → ℝ) (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) (ζ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (K : ℝ), W ⊆ U → T.massOn W ≠ ∞ → T.boundary.massOn W ≠ ∞ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ (k : ℕ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (ω : TestFormOn U k) (r : ℝ), S.massOn W ≠ ∞ → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ≤ r) → |S ω| ≤ r * (S.massOn W).toReal) → tsupport b ⊆ W → IsTestForm η → IsTestForm ζ → tsupport η ⊆ tsupport b → tsupport ζ ⊆ tsupport b → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (η x) ≤ K) → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ζ x) ≤ K) → (∀ x, exteriorDerivative η x = (b x * D x) • θ + ζ x) → |∫ x, b x * ξ x θ * D x ∂(μ.restrict W)| ≤ K * ((T.boundary.massOn W).toReal + (T.massOn W).toReal)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 4 (second to fourth bullets), with the divergence factor div g(q x) replaced by an arbitrary function D(x) and the evaluation bound eval_mass_bound taken as the hypothesis (EB).
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; M_W(S) := S.massOn W; ∂T := T.boundary ∈ 𝒟_m(U); μ⌞W := μ.restrict W. Hypotheses: (W) W ⊆ U; (M) M_W(T) ≠ ∞ and M_W(∂T) ≠ ∞; (R) T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for ω ∈ TestFormOn U (m+1); (EB) as in the statement; (b) tsupport b ⊆ W; (F) η, ζ are test forms with tsupport η ⊆ tsupport b, tsupport ζ ⊆ tsupport b, |η(x)| ≤ K and |ζ(x)| ≤ K for all x; (d) exteriorDerivative η x = (b(x)·D(x))•θ + ζ(x) for all x.
1. (Test forms in U.) By (F), (b) and (W), tsupport η ⊆ tsupport b ⊆ W ⊆ U and tsupport ζ ⊆ tsupport b ⊆ W ⊆ U. Since η and ζ are test forms, η' := ⟨η, ⟨IsTestForm η, tsupport η ⊆ U⟩⟩ ∈ TestFormOn U m and ζ' := ⟨ζ, ⟨IsTestForm ζ, tsupport ζ ⊆ U⟩⟩ ∈ TestFormOn U (m+1). Put ω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η' − ζ' ∈ TestFormOn U (m+1).
2. (The form ω.) By the definition of exteriorDerivativeTestOn, the underlying form of exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η' is exteriorDerivative η, and the coercion TestFormOn U (m+1) → DifferentialForm commutes with subtraction. Hence for every x, using (d): ω(x) = exteriorDerivative η x − ζ(x) = (b(x)·D(x))•θ.
3. (T(ω) through ∂T.) T.toCurrent is ℝ-linear, so T(ω) = T(exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η') − T(ζ'). (In Lean use map_sub for (T.toCurrent : TestFormOn U (m+1) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ); dot notation through the abbreviation CurrentOn may not resolve.) By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, which holds by rfl, T(exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η') = ∂T(η'). Thus T(ω) = ∂T(η') − T(ζ').
4. (Mass bounds.) Apply (EB) with k = m, S = ∂T, the form η' and r = K. Its hypotheses hold: M_W(∂T) ≠ ∞ by (M), tsupport η ⊆ W by step 1, and |η(x)| ≤ K by (F). So |∂T(η')| ≤ K·M_W(∂T).toReal. Apply (EB) with k = m+1, S = T, the form ζ' and r = K to get |T(ζ')| ≤ K·M_W(T).toReal. By |a − c| ≤ |a| + |c| and step 3, |T(ω)| ≤ K·M_W(∂T).toReal + K·M_W(T).toReal = K·(M_W(∂T).toReal + M_W(T).toReal).
5. (The integral equals T(ω).) Let F(x) := b(x)·ξ(x)(θ)·D(x).
 - By (R) and step 2, T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)((b(x)·D(x))•θ) dμ(x). Since ξ(x) is linear, ξ(x)((b(x)D(x))•θ) = (b(x)D(x))·ξ(x)(θ) = F(x) (map_smul, smul_eq_mul, ring). So T(ω) = ∫ F dμ.
 - If x ∉ W then x ∉ tsupport b by (b), so b(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and F(x) = 0.
 - Hence setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, which needs no measurability, gives ∫ F d(μ⌞W) = ∫_W F dμ = ∫ F dμ = T(ω).
6. (Conclusion.) By steps 4 and 5, |∫ b(x)·ξ(x)(θ)·D(x) d(μ⌞W)(x)| = |T(ω)| ≤ K·((T.boundary.massOn W).toReal + (T.massOn W).toReal).
proof_key_steps: η, ζ are test forms supported in tsupport b ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω := dη' − ζ' ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) has ω(x) = (b(x)D(x))•θ.
Linearity and boundary_apply give T(ω) = ∂T(η') − T(ζ').
(EB) bounds |∂T(η')| ≤ K M_W(∂T) and |T(ζ')| ≤ K M_W(T).
The representation turns T(ω) into ∫ b ξ(θ) D dμ, which equals the μ⌞W integral because b = 0 off W.

subproblems.title: Uniform divergence bounds and (TD) force f = 0 a.e. on W ∩ q⁻¹(N) (parent steps 5–6)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ ℝ^P open, μ a measure on ℝ^P with μ(W) < ∞, f : ℝ^P → ℝ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |f(x)| ≤ c for all x, q : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ (Euclid n) measurable and N ⊆ ℝⁿ measurable. For g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ write div g(y) := LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g y). Assume (TD): for every finite measure ν on ℝ^P, every ν-integrable h : ℝ^P → ℝ and every Λ ∈ ℝ such that |∫ h(x)·div g(q(x)) dν(x)| ≤ Λ for all C^∞ compactly supported g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with ‖g(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y, one has ∫_{q⁻¹(N)} h dν = 0. Assume (DB): for every C^∞ compactly supported b : ℝ^P → ℝ with tsupport b ⊆ W there is Λ_b ∈ ℝ with |∫ b(x)·f(x)·div g(q(x)) d(μ.restrict W)(x)| ≤ Λ_b for all C^∞ compactly supported g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with ‖g(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y. Then for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ W and q(x) ∈ N imply f(x) = 0. (C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞).)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (q : Euclid P → Euclid n) (N : Set (Euclid n)) (c : ℝ), IsOpen W → μ W < ∞ → AEStronglyMeasurable f μ → (∀ x, |f x| ≤ c) → Measurable q → MeasurableSet N → (∀ (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (h : Euclid P → ℝ) (Λ : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasure ν → Integrable h ν → (∀ g : Euclid n → Euclid n, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → |∫ x, h x * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g (q x)).toLinearMap ∂ν| ≤ Λ) → ∫ x in q ⁻¹' N, h x ∂ν = 0) → (∀ b : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) b → HasCompactSupport b → tsupport b ⊆ W → ∃ Λ : ℝ, ∀ g : Euclid n → Euclid n, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → |∫ x, b x * f x * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g (q x)).toLinearMap ∂(μ.restrict W)| ≤ Λ) → ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ W → q x ∈ N → f x = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 5 and 6, with f := ξ(·)(θ), q := q_I and N := q_I(C) abstracted. The top-dimensional lemma top_dim_null, specialized to X = ℝ^P, this q and this N, is the hypothesis (TD).
Notation: div g(y) := LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g y); ν_W := μ.restrict W; A := q⁻¹(N). Hypotheses: (W) W is open and μ(W) < ∞; (f) f is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and |f(x)| ≤ c for all x; (q) q is measurable and N is measurable; (TD) and (DB) as in the statement.
1. (Preliminaries.)
 - A is measurable, as the preimage of the measurable set N under the measurable map q.
 - ν_W(ℝ^P) = μ(W) < ∞, so ν_W is a finite measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict).
 - c ≥ |f(0)| ≥ 0.
2. (The function F.) Let F := A.indicator f, i.e. F(x) = f(x) for x ∈ A and F(x) = 0 otherwise.
 - F is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.indicator, A measurable).
 - ‖F(x)‖ ≤ c for every x: on A this is (f), off A it is 0 ≤ c.
 - Hence F is integrable for the finite measure ν_W (Integrable.of_bound applied to the restriction), i.e. IntegrableOn F W μ, and therefore LocallyIntegrableOn F W μ (IntegrableOn.locallyIntegrableOn).
3. (Vanishing of the localized integrals.) Let b : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport b ⊆ W.
 (a) b is continuous with compact support, hence bounded: there is B with |b(x)| ≤ B for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). Let h(x) := b(x)·f(x). h is ν_W-a.e. strongly measurable: b is continuous and f is ν_W-a.e. strongly measurable by (f) and AEStronglyMeasurable.restrict, so the product is (AEStronglyMeasurable.mul). Also |h(x)| ≤ B·c. So h is ν_W-integrable (Integrable.of_bound).
 (b) Let Λ_b be given by (DB) for b. (DB) states exactly |∫ h(x)·div g(q(x)) dν_W(x)| ≤ Λ_b for every C^∞ compactly supported g with ‖g‖ ≤ 1. So (TD), applied to ν := ν_W, this h and Λ := Λ_b, gives ∫_A b·f dν_W = 0.
 (c) For x ∉ W we have x ∉ tsupport b, so b(x) = 0 and b(x)·F(x) = 0. By setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, ∫ b(x)•F(x) dμ(x) = ∫_W b·F dμ = ∫ b·F dν_W.
 (d) Pointwise b(x)·F(x) = A.indicator (b·f)(x) (check x ∈ A and x ∉ A separately). By integral_indicator (A measurable), ∫ A.indicator (b·f) dν_W = ∫_A b·f dν_W = 0 by (b).
 (e) Hence ∫ b(x)•F(x) dμ(x) = 0.
4. (Localization.) By step 2 (local integrability of F on the open set W) and step 3 (for every such b), IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero gives: for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ W implies F(x) = 0.
5. (Conclusion.) Let x be one of these points with x ∈ W and q(x) ∈ N. Then x ∈ A, so f(x) = F(x) = 0. Hence for μ-a.e. x: x ∈ W → q(x) ∈ N → f(x) = 0.
proof_key_steps: μ⌞W is finite and A := q⁻¹(N) is measurable; F := 1_A f is bounded, hence locally integrable on W.
For each smooth compactly supported b ⊂ W, h := b f is μ⌞W-integrable and (DB)+(TD) give ∫_A b f d(μ⌞W) = 0.
Since b vanishes off W, ∫ b F dμ = ∫_A b f d(μ⌞W) = 0.
Mathlib's IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero gives F = 0 μ-a.e. on W, i.e. f = 0 a.e. on W ∩ q⁻¹(N).

subproblems.title: The mass measure vanishes where the orientation vanishes (parent step 8)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, W, C ⊆ ℝ^P with W and C measurable and C ⊆ W, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), μ a measure on ℝ^P with μ(W) < ∞ and T.massOn W = μ(W), and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n (MultiVector P n) with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α for all x and α and T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). If ξ(x) = 0 for μ-a.e. x ∈ C, then μ(C) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W C : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), MeasurableSet W → MeasurableSet C → C ⊆ W → μ W < ∞ → T.massOn W = μ W → (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ C → ξ x = 0) → μ C = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 8, for an arbitrary measurable W of finite μ-measure and measurable C ⊆ W.
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. M_W(T) := T.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, i.e. over ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. μ.real s := (μ s).toReal. Hypotheses: (S) W and C are measurable, C ⊆ W, μ(W) < ∞; (M) M_W(T) = μ(W); (5) |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|; (6) T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x); (Z) for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ C → ξ(x) = 0.
1. (The bound G.) μ(W∖C) ≤ μ(W) < ∞. G := (W∖C).indicator 1 is real-valued, G ≥ 0, and G is μ-integrable because W∖C is measurable of finite measure (integrable_indicator_iff, integrableOn_const). Also ∫ G dμ = μ.real(W∖C) (integral_indicator_one).
2. (Pointwise domination.) Fix ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W and let F(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)). Claim: ‖F(x)‖ ≤ G(x) for μ-a.e. x. Take any x for which the implication in (Z) holds.
 - If x ∈ C (so x ∈ W): ξ(x) = 0, so F(x) = 0 ≤ G(x).
 - If x ∈ W∖C: |F(x)| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1 = G(x), by (5) and admissibility.
 - If x ∉ W: x ∉ tsupport ω because tsupport ω ⊆ W. So ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and F(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0 ≤ G(x).
3. (Each admissible value.) By (6), T(ω) = ∫ F dμ. norm_integral_le_of_norm_le needs only G to be integrable, and gives T(ω) ≤ ‖∫ F dμ‖ ≤ ∫ G dμ = μ.real(W∖C). Hence ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ ofReal(μ.real(W∖C)) = μ(W∖C), the equality because μ(W∖C) ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
4. (Supremum.) ω was an arbitrary admissible form, so sSup_le gives M_W(T) ≤ μ(W∖C). By (M), μ(W) ≤ μ(W∖C).
5. (Conclusion.) C is measurable and C ⊆ W, so μ(W∖C) + μ(C) = μ(W∖C) + μ(W ∩ C) = μ(W) (measure_sdiff_add_inter). With step 4, μ(W∖C) + μ(C) ≤ μ(W∖C) + 0. Since μ(W∖C) < ∞, it may be cancelled (ENNReal.add_le_add_iff_left), so μ(C) ≤ 0, i.e. μ(C) = 0.
proof_key_steps: For admissible ω, |ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ 1_{W∖C}(x) μ-a.e.: it vanishes off W (ω = 0) and a.e. on C (ξ = 0), and is ≤ |ω| ≤ 1 on W∖C.
Hence T(ω) ≤ μ(W∖C), so μ(W) = M_W(T) ≤ μ(W∖C).

subproblems.title: Null sets: from compact subsets of U to arbitrary sets (parent step 9)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and μ, ν measures on ℝ^P (Euclid P) such that μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and μ(C) = 0 for every compact C ⊆ U with ν(C) = 0. Then μ(E) = 0 for every E ⊆ ℝ^P with ν(E) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → (∀ C : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact C → C ⊆ U → ν C = 0 → μ C = 0) → ∀ E : Set (Euclid P), ν E = 0 → μ E = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 9, with μHE[n] replaced by an arbitrary measure ν; only monotonicity of ν and the existence of measurable null hulls are used.
Hypotheses: (U) U is open; (1) μ(Uᶜ) = 0; (2) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; (C) μ(C) = 0 for every compact C ⊆ U with ν(C) = 0.
1. (Null hull.) Let E ⊆ ℝ^P with ν(E) = 0. By exists_measurable_superset_of_null there is a measurable E' ⊇ E with ν(E') = 0.
2. (Compact exhaustion of U.) By IsOpen.exists_iUnion_isClosed there are closed sets F_i ⊆ U (i ∈ ℕ) with ⋃_i F_i = U. For p = (i, j) ∈ ℕ × ℕ put K_p := F_i ∩ closedBall(0, j).
 - K_p is compact: it is a closed subset of the compact ball closedBall(0, j) in the proper space ℝ^P (isCompact_closedBall, IsCompact.inter_left).
 - K_p ⊆ F_i ⊆ U.
 - If x ∈ U, pick i with x ∈ F_i and a natural number j ≥ dist(x, 0) (exists_nat_ge). Then x ∈ K_{(i,j)}. Hence U ⊆ ⋃_p K_p.
3. (Each piece is null.) Fix p and write K := K_p.
 - By (2), μ(K) < ∞, so μ⌞K := μ.restrict K is a finite measure on ℝ^P (isFiniteMeasure_restrict).
 - A finite measure on ℝ^P is locally finite, hence regular (instance Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure), hence inner regular by compact sets on measurable sets of finite measure (Measure.InnerRegularCompactLTTop, found by instance search).
 - Suppose μ(E' ∩ K) ≠ 0. As E' is measurable, (μ⌞K)(E') = μ(E' ∩ K) > 0 (Measure.restrict_apply), and (μ⌞K)(E') < ∞.
 - MeasurableSet.exists_lt_isCompact_of_ne_top with r = 0 gives a compact C ⊆ E' with (μ⌞K)(C) > 0. C is closed, hence measurable, so (μ⌞K)(C) = μ(C ∩ K) > 0.
 - But C ∩ K is compact (C compact, K closed), C ∩ K ⊆ K ⊆ U, and ν(C ∩ K) ≤ ν(E') = 0 (measure_mono_null). So μ(C ∩ K) = 0 by (C), a contradiction.
 Therefore μ(E' ∩ K_p) = 0 for every p.
4. (Conclusion.) By step 2, E' ⊆ Uᶜ ∪ ⋃_p (E' ∩ K_p): a point of E' either lies outside U or lies in some K_p. By (1), step 3 and countable subadditivity over the countable index set ℕ × ℕ (measure_iUnion_null, measure_union_null), this union is μ-null. Hence μ(E) ≤ μ(E') = 0 (measure_mono_null), i.e. μ(E) = 0.
proof_key_steps: Replace E by a measurable ν-null hull E'.
Exhaust U by countably many compact sets K_{i,j} = F_i ∩ closedBall(0, j).
Each μ⌞K_{i,j} is finite, hence inner regular; a compact C ⊆ E' of positive μ(C ∩ K_{i,j}) would contradict the compact-set hypothesis, so μ(E' ∩ K_{i,j}) = 0.
